claims.text: The initial lightweight HEA has a homogeneous, uniform elemental distribution.
Rapid solidification or laser melting can induce coherent nanoscale precipitates in the proposed lightweight HEA.
Slower cooling of the same composition yields a more homogeneous microstructure with minimal precipitate formation.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates can increase alloy strength while retaining or increasing tensile ductility.
The nanoprecipitates strengthen the alloy by impeding dislocation movement.
The nanoscale features impart solid-solution strengthening.
Locating coherent nanoprecipitates particularly at grain boundaries is important for the proposed property synergy.
Coherent nanoprecipitates limit the diffusion of corrosive species and oxygen.
Diffusion obstruction by nanoprecipitates stabilizes a protective oxide scale at high temperature.
Precipitate engineering can simultaneously provide low density, strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The precipitate-containing rapidly processed alloy will have higher yield strength than the slowly cooled baseline.
The precipitate-containing rapidly processed alloy will have greater ductility than the slowly cooled baseline.
The precipitate-containing rapidly processed alloy will have a lower saline corrosion rate than the slowly cooled baseline.
The precipitate-containing rapidly processed alloy will have lower high-temperature oxidation weight gain than the slowly cooled baseline.
The precipitate-containing microstructure maintains a low-density matrix.
Failure to form stable coherent nanoprecipitates eliminates the predicted improvements in strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Coarsening of the nanoprecipitates eliminates the predicted improvements in strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.

contradictions.description: The design requires the treatment and control to differ in coherent-precipitate formation, but the rule treats finding similar precipitates in both conditions as falsification. That result would instead indicate failure of the intervention or manipulation check and would not test the proposed precipitate mechanism.
